AgentConfigCodex.description:
The `codex:` block — run this agent on OpenAI's Codex CLI instead of
Claude Code. Declaring the block at all is what selects the harness
(`AgentConfig.harness`).

Deliberately a small subset of `AgentConfigClaude`: the fields omitted here
are ones Codex has no equivalent for (`effort`, `fallback_model`,
`settings`) or that the platform does not yet wire through for this harness
(`max_turns`, `skills`, MCP servers). They are omitted rather than
accepted-and-ignored, because `StrictConfigModel` forbids extra keys — so a
config that sets one fails loudly at parse time instead of silently not doing
it. The budget still bounds a run regardless.
AgentConfigCodex.title: AgentConfigCodex

AgentConfigCompute.description:
Sandbox compute sizing. Every field is optional; None inherits the
platform default (1 vCPU / 4096 MiB / 3600s — see DEFAULT_MODAL_* in
models/ellipsis/sandboxes/sandbox.py). A resolved value outside the platform
bounds fails validation loudly (a sync error on the config) rather than
being clamped silently.

`memory` and `timeout` each accept a shorthand string ("8GB", "30m") or an
explicit units object ({gb: 8}, {minutes: 30}); the `memory_mib` /
`timeout_seconds` properties resolve either form to the canonical integer
the sandbox driver consumes.

`timeout` is the max wall-clock the agent may run before the sandbox is
killed, capped at 1h (MAX_SANDBOX_TIMEOUT_SECONDS — equal to the default, so
today the knob only shortens a session; the cap matches the 1-hour validity
of the sandbox's GitHub token). The worker's lease/visibility heartbeat
ceiling is derived from that cap, so a run at the max stays owned by its
worker for its whole life.

Compute is billed on the requested allocation over the sandbox's
wall-clock lifetime, so a bigger/longer box costs proportionally more.
AgentConfigCompute.title: AgentConfigCompute

AgentConfigDuration.description:
A duration as explicit units, summed. Set any of `hours`/`minutes`/
`seconds` (at least one). The alternative to the `30m`-style shorthand
string wherever a duration is accepted.
AgentConfigDuration.title: AgentConfigDuration

AgentConfigEllipsis.description:
The Ellipsis product namespace for a config file: which schema this is
(`version`), the human-facing identity (`name`/`description`), freeform
organizational `metadata`, whether the agent is `enabled`, and the
human-access flag `interactive`. The presence of a top-level `ellipsis:`
mapping is what marks a YAML file as an Ellipsis agent config (vs arbitrary
YAML that merely lives under a config directory) — see
`yaml_is_ellipsis_config`.

`enabled`/`interactive` are agent behavior, not freeform metadata, so they
stay inside the config `sha` (only `metadata` is sha-excluded).
`interactive` lets a human `agent session connect` to a live session (CLI
relay). It does not decide whether a session is ephemeral or durable — that
is the trigger's job.
AgentConfigEllipsis.title: AgentConfigEllipsis

AgentConfigEllipsisPermissions.description:
`permissions.ellipsis` as a map: resource → level | grant | list of
grants. Levels are hierarchical (read < write < delete), so `write`
includes `read`. An unlisted resource is denied. The whole block is
intersected with the platform's sandbox ceiling at token mint — it can
narrow what a sandbox token may do, never exceed it.
AgentConfigEllipsisPermissions.title: AgentConfigEllipsisPermissions

AgentConfigEnvironment.description:
Everything about the environment (the sandbox) the agent runs in: which
`repositories` are cloned into it, which environment `variables` it gets,
its `compute` sizing, how its `image` is customized, and lifecycle `hooks`.
What the agent may *do* from that environment is the top-level
`permissions:` block, not this one.

Each `variables` entry names a variable to inject; with an inline `value` it
is hardcoded, without one it is resolved from the account's sandbox-secrets
store. Only the named variables reach this agent; the rest of the account's
stored variables never do. This is how a config brings in the config and
credentials a custom CLI needs.
AgentConfigEnvironment.title: AgentConfigEnvironment

AgentConfigEnvironmentHooks.description:
Shell scripts run at points in the sandbox lifecycle, each as the sandbox
user with the sandbox's environment variables available. A non-zero exit
fails the run (exit_status = LIFECYCLE_HOOK_FAILED) and is not retried.

`post_start` runs after the container starts, before any repo is cloned —
repo-independent setup (authenticate a CLI, e.g. `doppler setup`). On Modal
the repo is baked into the image so it is incidentally present, but
`post_start` must not depend on repo contents (that's `post_clone`).

`post_clone` runs after all repos are cloned/checked out, before the agent —
repo-dependent setup (`pip install -r requirements.txt`, codegen).

Hooks run on every run and their output is never cached. A dependency
install whose result should be reused across runs belongs in `image.setup`
(baked into the cached image) instead; keep hooks for per-run work — e.g.
anything that touches run-scoped credentials.
AgentConfigEnvironmentHooks.title: AgentConfigEnvironmentHooks

AgentConfigEnvironmentImage.description:
How to customize the container image the agent runs in. You
contribute appended layers (`dockerfile_append`) and a build-time script
(`setup`) only — Ellipsis owns FROM / base tooling / entrypoint / user.
Today only inline bodies are supported; a file reference (resolved at the
run's SHA) will come later.

The split: `dockerfile_append` runs when the image is assembled, before any
repo exists — toolchain installs (a package manager binary, apt packages).
`setup` runs at image-build time *after* the configured repositories are
checked out, and its output is captured by the filesystem snapshot that
becomes the cached image — dependency installs (`poetry install`,
`npm install`), so later runs start with deps already on disk. Neither runs
per run; that's `hooks.post_start` / `hooks.post_clone`.
AgentConfigEnvironmentImage.title: AgentConfigEnvironmentImage

AgentConfigEnvironmentVariable.description:
One environment variable injected into the agent's sandbox.

`value`, when set, is a literal injected as-is — use it for non-secret
config (LOG_LEVEL, an API base URL). When `value` is omitted the value is
resolved at run time from the account's sandbox-secrets store (dashboard
/ `PUT /v1/secrets`) by `name`, so a secret can be injected without
ever putting it in the config file. Either way the variable only reaches
agents that name it.
AgentConfigEnvironmentVariable.title: AgentConfigEnvironmentVariable

AgentConfigGithubPermissions.description:
The agent's GitHub access: the scope of the installation token minted for
its sandbox — the credential `git`, `gh`, and the GitHub MCP server
authenticate with.

By default the token carries the installation's full permissions on all of
the installation's repositories. `permissions` narrows what it may do:
the string `read_only` grants read access to contents, issues, metadata and
pull requests; a map requests explicit levels per GitHub App permission
scope (e.g. `{contents: read, pull_requests: write}`) and may never exceed
what the installation granted. `repositories` scopes the token to exactly
the listed repos, by name (they must belong to the installation).

Restriction is enforced by GitHub, not by Ellipsis: the token itself is
minted with the reduced scope, so nothing running in the sandbox can
exceed it.
AgentConfigGithubPermissions.title: AgentConfigGithubPermissions

AgentConfigInput.description:
The typed input contract: what goes INTO a session (the trigger is
when it happens; this is what goes in).

`json_schema` types the payload a caller-started session takes
(`POST /v1/sessions` `input`, validated at the door; required when
declared). It is illegal on a react-triggered agent — react payloads are
platform-shaped (the published surface field sets), not caller-shaped.

`message` is the initial-message template: exact `{{path}}` substitution
over the caller payload (or, on a react agent, over the surface's
published fields), no conditionals/loops/filters. Refs are validated at
deploy time against the governing field set (see AgentConfig's
`_check_input`).
AgentConfigInput.title: AgentConfigInput

AgentConfigLlm.description:
Where this agent's completions go.

Defaults to Ellipsis's own LLM proxy (our Anthropic/Bedrock account, or the
account-wide BYO provider if one is enabled). Setting `proxy` to the id of a
proxy registered on the models settings page routes THIS agent's
completions through that gateway instead.

Opt-in per agent by design: registering a proxy does not silently move any
existing agent's traffic. The id is account-scoped, so naming another
account's id is a terminal config error, not a route.
AgentConfigLlm.title: AgentConfigLlm

AgentConfigMcpServer.description:
One built-in MCP server this agent opts into by name (`linear`/`slack`).
This is a name reference over the connected built-in set, NOT a custom-server
definition — there is no command/url/headers shape (that was the old,
removed field, and Ellipsis does not support bring-your-own MCP servers).
It only matters when the named integration is set to `opt_in` inclusion; an
integration in the default `all_sessions` mode is added regardless.
AgentConfigMcpServer.title: AgentConfigMcpServer

AgentConfigMemorySize.description:
A memory size as explicit units, summed (binary: 1GB = 1024MB = 1024MiB).
Set any of `gb`/`mb` (at least one). The alternative to the `8GB`-style
shorthand string.
AgentConfigMemorySize.title: AgentConfigMemorySize

AgentConfigMentionPlatform.description: The surface an @ellipsis mention can come from.
AgentConfigMentionPlatform.title: AgentConfigMentionPlatform

AgentConfigOutput.description:
The typed output contract: the JSON Schema the agent must exit through
(the StructuredOutput exit tool). Read back via
GET /v1/sessions/{id}/output.
AgentConfigOutput.title: AgentConfigOutput

AgentConfigPermissions.description:
What the agent is allowed to touch, per credential the platform mints
into its sandbox. Distinct from `environment:`, which is where the agent
runs; this is what it may do from there.

`ellipsis` scopes the sandbox's Ellipsis API token
(`ELLIPSIS_API_TOKEN`, what the in-sandbox `agent` CLI authenticates
with). `true` / the string `all` (the default) grant the full sandbox
ceiling — everything a sandbox token can ever do. A map narrows it per
resource (see `AgentConfigEllipsisPermissions`); the minted token carries
the intersection, so a config can only ever reduce access. `false` fails
validation — an agent with no API token cannot report its own progress.

`github` scopes the sandbox's GitHub installation token (`GH_TOKEN`) —
see `AgentConfigGithubPermissions`. GitHub enforces it at mint time.
AgentConfigPermissions.title: AgentConfigPermissions

AgentConfigSettingsRef.description:
A config-declared Claude Code settings.json, resolved at run start and
passed to `claude --settings <path>`. That is the CLI settings tier — BELOW
Ellipsis's managed-settings.json floor — so it customizes behavior (model
permissions, includeCoAuthoredBy, statusLine, ...) but can never weaken a
security setting. Lets a team point the cloud agent at the same settings file
they already use with Claude Code locally instead of re-encoding it as YAML.
AgentConfigSettingsRef.title: AgentConfigSettingsRef

AgentConfigSkill.description:
One config-declared Claude Code skill: a repository directory containing
a SKILL.md, resolved at run start and installed at the sandbox's personal
skill level (`~/.claude/skills/<basename(path)>/`). This is how a config
brings in skills its cloned repositories don't provide — cross-repo refs
(an org-wide skills repo), public third-party repos, and repo-less runs.
Skills under a cloned repo's own `.claude/skills/` load by themselves and
don't need an entry here.
AgentConfigSkill.title: AgentConfigSkill

AgentConfigSource.description:
Where a session's config came from. Total: every session has exactly one
source, including the ones that never touch defaults resolution.

Not derivable from the row — `agent_config_id` says WHICH saved config, not
how it was chosen, and is null for inline, platform-default, and built-in
configs alike — so it is persisted for audit and the published wire.
AgentConfigSource.title: AgentConfigSource

BudgetSource.description:
Which layer actually determined the enforced budget.

Not derivable from the run row alone (the run does not store the config
cents or the account default), so we persist it for the UI / audit.
BudgetSource.title: BudgetSource

DeltaFrame.description:
Fire-and-forget partial assistant output for the current response.
Carries no sequence number and is never resumable; superseded by the
committed record.

agent_turn_id.description: Identifier of the turn the delta belongs to, if known.
agent_turn_id.title: Agent Turn Id

kind.description: What the partial text is. Known values: text ('thinking' reserved). Open vocabulary: ignore deltas with unknown kinds.

output_tokens.description: Output tokens generated so far for the current response.
output_tokens.title: Output Tokens

DeltaFrame.title: DeltaFrame

DoneFrame.description:
Terminal marker: the conversation is over, after the final session
frame carried the end state. Followed by a normal close (1000).
DoneFrame.title: DoneFrame

EllipsisGrant.description:
One grant entry: a level, optionally narrowed to instances whose
natural key (a file's name, a memory's path, a secret's name, a config's
name, a session's id) matches any of the `match` globs.
EllipsisGrant.title: EllipsisGrant

ErrorFrame.description: Terminal error marker, sent before the server closes with code 1011.
ErrorFrame.title: ErrorFrame

anyOf.description:
One include-minus-exclude set of GitHub accounts: an account matches iff
it is in `include` (`true` = all, a list = exactly those, `false`/`[]` =
none) AND not in `exclude`. A bare bool or list is shorthand for `include`,
so `users: true` and `users: [priya-shah]` both parse.
anyOf.title: GithubAccountFilter

GithubAccountSelector.description:
A selector of GitHub accounts — the `for:` audience gate on react
surfaces and code review pipelines, classified on the stable entity author
(the pusher for `push`, the PR author for a review). `users` selects human
accounts, `bots` selects bot accounts; each is a `GithubAccountFilter`
(include minus exclude, with bare bool/list shorthand).
GithubAccountSelector.title: GithubAccountSelector

GithubAccountSnippet.description:
Sometimes the GitHub API returns a user of github (can include bots)
using this snippet instead of the full GithubAccount model. One example,
is when the API returns a pull request.

This is the least amount of info we need to represent a GitHub account.
GithubAccountSnippet.title: GithubAccountSnippet

HeartbeatFrame.description:
A keepalive sent after a period of idleness; doubles as the dead-socket
probe. Clients should treat roughly twice the heartbeat interval of
silence as a dead connection.

ts.description: Server time when the heartbeat was sent.
ts.title: Ts

HeartbeatFrame.title: HeartbeatFrame

Level.description:
What may be done to a resource. Strictly ordered: a grant at one level
includes every level below it (write-only would be a phantom capability —
no real client can create what it cannot read back).
Level.title: Level

ParentKind.description:
How a session relates to its predecessor (parent_agent_session_id) —
the ONE "preceded-by" chain for every predecessor relationship. Routing
reads this when the distinction matters.

CONTINUATION — a follow-up in the same conversation surface (e.g. a Slack
thread reply spawning a fresh session on the same thread).
RESUME — a conversation re-hosted on a new box after its sandbox was torn
down (interactive platform; later phase).
ParentKind.title: ParentKind

PromptBlockedReason.description: Why direct prompting is refused. Absent when prompting is allowed.
PromptBlockedReason.title: PromptBlockedReason

RecordsAppendFrame.description:
Cursored append-only delivery of session records, ordered by feed_seq,
from all sources. Every record in the frame advances the resume cursor —
including ones a client renders as nothing.

records.description: New session records, ordered by feed_seq.
records.title: Records

RecordsAppendFrame.title: RecordsAppendFrame

anyOf.description:
The watch scope of a trigger, by repository name (owner defaults to the
account). Include minus exclude: `include: []` (the default) covers every
repository of the installation, so `exclude`-only means "all except these"
and keeps covering repositories added to the org later. A bare list is
shorthand for `include`.
anyOf.title: RepositoryFilter

Resource.description:
Everything a credential can be granted access to, one value per /v1
resource family. `TOKENS` is reserved for the future token-management
routes; nothing maps to it yet.
Resource.title: Resource

RunStatus.description: What the current (or most recent) execution is doing (backs `run`).
RunStatus.title: RunStatus

Session.description:
An agent session: one conversation with an agent, from trigger to
terminal state. Returned by `GET /v1/sessions/{id}` and carried by the
session stream's `session`/`snapshot` frames — REST and stream never
disagree about what a session looks like.

agent.description: The agent that ran: the config the session executed, where that config came from, and any override merged into it.

attribution.description: The principal this session is attributed to.

budget.description: The spend budget enforced for this session.

context_repository.description: The "owner/name" repository context the session was started in, if any.
context_repository.title: Context Repository

cost.description: What the session cost, in millicents, broken down by leg and carrying its own total.

exit_status.description: How the session ended; null until it is terminal.

harness.description: The coding-agent harness the session runs on.

last_activity_at.description: When the session last showed activity.
last_activity_at.title: Last Activity At

last_message_at.description: When the session last received a message.
last_message_at.title: Last Message At

output_prs.description: Pull requests the session created or updated.
output_prs.title: Output Prs

parent.description: What preceded this session, if anything.

prompt.description: The per-session prompt the session was started with.
prompt.title: Prompt

prompting.description: Whether a client may send this session a message and, when it may not, the reason to show instead of a composer.

session_state.description: Lifecycle state of the durable conversation, or null for sessions without one.

source.description: Where the session came from (e.g. react, manual, api, cli, mention, cron).

status_reason.description: Human-readable reason for the current status, when there is one.
status_reason.title: Status Reason

stopped.description: The stop request, if the session was stopped.

summary.description: The latest live summary of the session's progress while it runs, and when it was generated.

surface.description: The public status projection; null on list/search responses, which do not derive it.

tokens.description: The tokens the session spent and the model they went to. `total` includes the prompt-cache lanes.

updated_at.description: When the session was last updated.
updated_at.title: Updated At

Session.title: Session

SessionAgent.description:
The agent this session ran: the config it actually executed, where that
config came from, and the diff that was merged in — the same
effective-value-plus-provenance shape `SessionBudget` uses.

`config` is the snapshot frozen when the session was created; `config_id`
points at the saved config as it exists NOW. They diverge legitimately: a
YAML edit after the session started, or any `override`, leaves the pointer
describing something the session never ran.

config.description: The agent config the session actually ran, frozen when the session was created.

config_id.description: Identifier of the saved config this session's snapshot was taken from. Null for inline, platform-default, and built-in configs. Points at the config as it exists now, which may have changed since.
config_id.title: Config Id

override.description: The partial-config override merged into `config` for this session, or null when the config ran unmodified. `config` is the merged result; this is the diff.
override.title: Override

source.description: How this session's config was chosen.

SessionAgent.title: SessionAgent

SessionAttribution.description:
The principal a session is attributed to: what kind, its id, and — when
the kind is a GitHub user — the resolved display snippet.

id.description: Identifier of the principal the session is attributed to.
id.title: Id

type.description: Kind of principal the session is attributed to (e.g. a GitHub user or an API key).

user.description: The GitHub user the session is attributed to, resolved at read time. Null when the attribution is not a GitHub user.

SessionAttribution.title: SessionAttribution

SessionBudget.description:
The spend budget actually enforced for this session, and which layer of
the cascade set it.

cents.description: The spend budget resolved for this session, in cents.
cents.title: Cents

source.description: Where the resolved budget came from.

SessionBudget.title: SessionBudget

SessionCost.description:
What a session (or one turn of it) cost, in millicents.

`llm` is deliberately NOT called `tokens`: it would sit beside the `tokens`
object and read as "the token count's cost" rather than "the cost of the
LLM leg".

total.description: The grand total in millicents: llm + sandbox_cpu + sandbox_memory + fee.
total.title: Total

SessionCost.title: SessionCost

SessionExitStatus.description:
Why a terminal agent session ended — a finer-grained reason than `status`.

`status` (SessionStatus) is the lifecycle state: COMPLETED / ERROR /
CANCELLED. `exit_status` explains *why* a run reached that terminal state, so
the UI and metrics can tell a budget cutoff apart from a crashed tool call or
a deliberate cancellation. It is None until the run reaches a terminal state.
SessionExitStatus.title: SessionExitStatus

SessionFrame.description:
A last-writer-wins snapshot of the session — the only way status,
state, and cost updates arrive. Resent whole on any field change.
SessionFrame.title: SessionFrame

SessionLiveness.description: The durable conversation axis (backs the surfaced `session` field).
SessionLiveness.title: SessionLiveness

SessionMessage.description:
One message in a session's inbox: what a queued message renders and
retires on. The webhook provenance internals stay off the wire.

author.description: Display attribution of the message's sender.
author.title: Author

delivered_at.description: When the message was delivered to the agent, if it has been.
delivered_at.title: Delivered At

delivered_turn_id.description: Identifier of the turn the message was delivered into, if any.
delivered_turn_id.title: Delivered Turn Id

feed_seq.description: Where the message sits in the session's feed — placement metadata only, NOT a resume cursor (only records_append frames advance the cursor). Null for older rows.
feed_seq.title: Feed Seq

sender_attribution_id.description: Identifier of the principal that sent the message, if attributed.
sender_attribution_id.title: Sender Attribution Id

sender_attribution_type.description: Kind of principal that sent the message, if attributed.

session_id.description: Identifier of the session the message belongs to.
session_id.title: Session Id

SessionMessage.title: SessionMessage

SessionParent.description:
The ONE "preceded-by" chain: the predecessor session and how this one
relates to it. Not a parent that orchestrates children — a session never
spawns sub-sessions.

kind.description: How this session relates to its parent session, if any.

replayed_from_session_id.description: Identifier of the original session this one was replayed from, if it was started via replay.
replayed_from_session_id.title: Replayed From Session Id

session_id.description: Identifier of the parent session that spawned this one, if any.
session_id.title: Session Id

SessionParent.title: SessionParent

SessionPr.description:
A pull request this session created, denormalized at capture time so
session surfaces render a labeled link without joining gh_prs. Live PR
state (open/merged/closed) is not stored here — read it from gh_prs where
a view needs it.
SessionPr.title: SessionPr

SessionPrompting.description:
The prompt-affordance projection. `enabled` answers "would a send work",
and when it wouldn't, `blocked_reason` + `detail` say why.

`surface_name` is set only for MENTION_SURFACE, naming where to reply.
SessionPrompting.title: SessionPrompting

SessionRecord.description:
One entry of a session's log: a stable envelope around the harness's
native payload. Internal-only columns are deliberately absent so internal
model evolution stays free.

agent_turn_id.description: Identifier of the turn the record belongs to, if any.
agent_turn_id.title: Agent Turn Id

cost.description: Cost attributed to this record, if any.
cost.title: Cost

duration.description: Duration attributed to this record, if any.
duration.title: Duration

feed_seq.description: The record's position in the session's ordered feed — the resume cursor for the stream and the records endpoints.
feed_seq.title: Feed Seq

model.description: The model that produced this record, if any.
model.title: Model

payload.description: The harness's native line, verbatim. Consumers parse it at their own risk, versioned via record_format.
payload.title: Payload

record_format.description: Versions the payload shape, e.g. claude_stream_json@2.0 or ellipsis_lifecycle@1.
record_format.title: Record Format

record_type.description: The record's type within its format.
record_type.title: Record Type

session_id.description: Identifier of the session the record belongs to.
session_id.title: Session Id

session_message_id.description: Correlates a user-echo record back to the session message it echoes, so clients can retire queued messages by id.
session_message_id.title: Session Message Id

source.description: Who wrote the record. Known values: claude_code (a native harness transcript record) | lifecycle (a platform notification). Open vocabulary: ignore records with unknown sources.

stream_seq.description: The record's position within its execution's stream.
stream_seq.title: Stream Seq

tokens_info.description: Token usage reported for this record, if any.

tools.description: Names of the tools used in this record, if any.
tools.title: Tools

SessionRecord.title: SessionRecord

SessionState.description:
Lifecycle of a keyed (multi-turn) session — the durable conversation.
Distinct from SessionStatus, which is per-execution (one turn's run) and
moves to agent_turns in a later slice. IDLE: alive, waiting for the next
message. RUNNING: a turn is executing. CLOSED: the conversation is done and
its sandbox/snapshots are torn down.
SessionState.title: SessionState

SessionStopped.description:
The stop request, if there was one: when, by which GitHub account id,
and that account resolved to a display snippet.

at.description: When a stop was requested, if one was.
at.title: At

by.description: GitHub account id of the user who stopped the session, if known.
by.title: By

by_user.description: The GitHub user who stopped the session, resolved at read time.

SessionStopped.title: SessionStopped

SessionSummary.description:
A live one-line summary of what the session is working on, refreshed
every few steps while it runs.

created_at.description: When this summary line was generated. Null on summaries written before generation time was tracked.
created_at.title: Created At

description.description: One-line description of what the session is working on.
description.title: Description

SessionSummary.title: SessionSummary

SessionSurface.description:
The three fields we expose.

`use_enum_values=True` (from CustomBaseModel) stores the members as their
string values, so this serializes to `{"session": "alive", "run": "waiting",
"status": "waiting"}` — a plain object, not enum names.
SessionSurface.title: SessionSurface

SessionTokens.description:
The token counts a session (or turn) spent, and the model they went to.

`total` INCLUDES the cache lanes, unlike the old flat `tokens_total` which
counted input+output+thinking only and left callers to add cache reads and
writes back themselves (the deleted `tokensTotalAll` helper). Cache tokens
dominate an agent run's token bill, so a "total" that omits them is the
wrong default and produced two competing totals in the dashboard.

cache_creation.description: Tokens written to the prompt cache.
cache_creation.title: Cache Creation

cache_read.description: Tokens read from the prompt cache.
cache_read.title: Cache Read

model.description: The model the token counts are attributed to.
model.title: Model

total.description: Total tokens consumed, INCLUDING the prompt-cache reads and writes — the same basis the token cost is priced on.
total.title: Total

SessionTokens.title: SessionTokens

SnapshotFrame.description:
The first frame after the stream connects: the session plus its open
inbox. Records always arrive separately via records_append frames.

earliest_feed_seq.description: The retention head: the lowest feed_seq still stored for this session, or null when it has no stored records. A client resuming from after_seq < earliest_feed_seq - 1 knows history is truncated.
earliest_feed_seq.title: Earliest Feed Seq

protocol.description: Echoes the protocol version the server is serving.
protocol.title: Protocol

SnapshotFrame.title: SnapshotFrame

TokensInfo.description:
Token/cost usage, per record (one API call's counts, aggregate fields at
their zero defaults) or aggregated per execution/session
(compute_spend_from_records derives num_turns and cost_usd).

Strict on purpose: this is our own persisted schema, so an unknown key is a
writer bug (the num_turns=0 bug shipped because a Claude Code usage dict
validated leniently against this model, silently zeroing every
non-overlapping field). Legacy keys were dropped from persisted blobs by
